text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- Danish banks have some of the world's best computer systems, offering the likelihood of handsome earnings in sales of know-how to foreign banks.
--- Foreign banks have difficulties getting into the Danish market as 47 percent of all Danes would never consider becoming customers of a foreign bank, a new survey shows.

--- Minister of justice Frank Jensen has political support for banning Nazi organisations after this weekend's letter bombs sent by Danish suspected neo-Nazis to targets in Britain, but leading criminal law experts doubt that a ban would have any effect and the police intelligence service say it has no proof that Nazis are a criminal organisation.
--- Denmark is to have almost 200 more discount cash and carry stores within the next three years, surpassing all previous forecasts.
--- Preventing breakdowns through better machine maintenance could save Danish companies 30 million crowns a year, new estimates show.
--- Housing prices are seen rising by 10 percent this year and the development is to continue in years to come, leading economists and bankers estimate.

--- Finance minister Mogens Lykketoft foresees a future lack of Danes over 60 years old on the labour market and believes that this will make them work for a longer period, hereby taking the pressure of state pension expenses.
